question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A government or society in which rulers use their power to steal the country's resources.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Kleptocracy.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Kleptocracy" means a government whose rulers use their power to steal the nation's wealth and resources, from the Greek “kleptes” (thief) and “kratos” (rule, power). (चोरों का शासन)
◦ Example: Critics accused the regime of running a kleptocracy rather than a democracy.

 

• The suffix "-cracy" always denotes rule or government by, and the first part of the word tells us who or what governs.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Plutocracy (धनिकतंत्र): Government by the wealthy, from the Greek “ploutos” (wealth).

 

• Option 2: Meritocracy (योग्यतातंत्र): A system in which power is held by those with the greatest ability or merit.

 

• Option 4: Gerontocracy (वृद्धतंत्र): A government ruled by the elders of a society.

 

NOTE

 

• Other "-cracy" words frequently asked in SSC: Plutocracy (the wealthy), Meritocracy (those with merit), Gerontocracy (the elders), Theocracy (religious leaders), Autocracy (a single ruler) and Bureaucracy (government officials).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Hedonist (सुखवादी): One who believes pleasure is life's chief goal

2. Sybarite (विलासप्रिय व्यक्ति): A person devoted to luxury and pleasure

3. Gourmet (स्वाद-विशेषज्ञ): A connoisseur of fine food and drink

4. Bon vivant (जीवन-रसिक व्यक्ति): One who enjoys a sociable, luxurious lifestyle

5. Philatelist (डाक-टिकट संग्रहकर्ता): A person who collects postage stamps

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A person who takes particular pleasure in fine food and drink.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Epicure.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Epicure" means a person who takes particular pleasure in fine food and drink, named after the Greek philosopher Epicurus, who taught that pleasure was the highest good. (स्वाद-प्रिय व्यक्ति)
◦ Example: As a true epicure, he could tell which vineyard a wine came from with a single sip.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Gourmand (स्वादलोलुप / खाऊ): A person who enjoys eating, often to excess.

 

• Option 2: Ascetic (तपस्वी): A person who practises strict self-denial, especially for religious reasons.

 

• Option 3: Glutton (पेटू): A person who eats or drinks excessively.

 

NOTE

 

• Other words close in meaning to "Epicure" frequently asked in SSC: Gourmet (a connoisseur of fine food and drink), Gastronome (an expert in good eating), Bon vivant (one who enjoys a luxurious, sociable life), Hedonist (one who pursues pleasure as life's chief goal) and Sybarite (a person fond of luxury).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Numismatist (सिक्का संग्रहकर्ता): A person who collects or studies coins

2. Ornithologist (पक्षी विज्ञानी): A person who studies birds

3. Entomologist (कीट विज्ञानी): A person who studies insects

4. Archaeologist (पुरातत्वविद): A person who studies history through excavation

5. Genealogist (वंशावली विशेषज्ञ): A person who traces family lineages

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A person who believes that all events are predetermined by fate and are therefore inevitable.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Fatalist.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Fatalist" means a person who believes that all events are predetermined by fate and cannot be changed, from the Latin “fatum” (that which is spoken, fate). (भाग्यवादी व्यक्ति)
◦ Example: Being a fatalist, he never worried about the outcome of the exam.

 

• The suffix "-ist" often denotes a person who believes in or practises something, and the first part of the word tells us what that belief or practice is.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: Optimist (आशावादी): A person who tends to expect the best possible outcome.

 

• Option 3: Pessimist (निराशावादी): A person who tends to expect the worst possible outcome.

 

• Option 4: Stoic (आत्मसंयमी): A person who endures hardship without complaint or show of feeling.

 

NOTE

 

• Other "-ist" words denoting a believer or follower frequently asked in SSC: Optimist (one who expects the best), Pessimist (one who expects the worst), Altruist (one concerned for others' welfare), Egoist (one concerned chiefly with self-interest) and Atheist (one who denies the existence of God).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Etymologist (शब्द-व्युत्पत्ति विज्ञानी): A person who studies the origin of words

2. Cartographer (मानचित्रकार): A person who draws or makes maps

3. Choreographer (नृत्य रचनाकार): A person who designs the steps of a dance

4. Calligrapher (सुलेखक): A person skilled in decorative handwriting

5. Ventriloquist (बोली फेंकने वाला कलाकार): A performer who speaks without moving their lips

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A person who is excessively concerned with minor details, rules, or formal points of learning.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Pedant.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Pedant" means a person who is excessively concerned with minor details or formal rules of learning. (आडंबरपूर्ण विद्वान)
◦ Example: The editor was a pedant who corrected even the smallest punctuation error.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Dilettante (शौकिया विद्वान): A person with only a superficial or amateur interest in a subject.

 

• Option 3: Polymath (बहुज्ञ): A person of great and varied learning across many subjects.

 

• Option 4: Connoisseur (पारखी): An expert judge in matters of taste, especially in the fine arts.

 

NOTE

 

• Other words close in meaning to "Pedant" frequently asked in SSC: Purist (a stickler for correctness and tradition), Precisian (one who is excessively precise about rules), Doctrinaire (one who applies theory without regard to practicality), Stickler (a person who insists on a certain quality/behaviour) and Dogmatist (one who asserts opinions dogmatically).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Eulogy (प्रशंसा-भाषण / श्रद्धांजलि): A speech praising someone who has died

2. Elegy (शोक गीत): A mournful poem, typically for the dead

3. Cenotaph (स्मृति-स्तंभ): A monument honouring the dead buried elsewhere

4. Obituary (मृत्यु सूचना): A published notice of a person's death

5. Panegyric (प्रशंसा-भाषण): A public speech or writing in praise of someone

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

To run away secretly, typically in order to avoid arrest or escape a difficult situation.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Abscond.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Abscond" means to run away secretly, typically to avoid arrest or legal consequences, from the Latin “ab” (away) and “condere” (to hide). (फरार होना)
◦ Example: The accused absconded before the police could arrest him.

 

• The prefix "ab-" (from Latin, meaning “away from”) appears in several SSC-relevant words such as abstain, abdicate, and aberrant, generally signalling movement or deviation away from something.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Elope (भाग जाना): To run away secretly, especially to get married without permission.

 

• Option 2: Deport (निर्वासित करना): To expel a foreigner from a country, usually for illegal presence or conduct.

 

• Option 4: Extradite (प्रत्यर्पण करना): To hand over an accused or convicted person to another country or authority for trial.

 

NOTE

 

• Other words close in meaning to "Abscond" frequently asked in SSC: Elope (run away secretly to marry), Decamp (leave suddenly and secretly), Skedaddle (run away hurriedly), Bolt (run away suddenly), Flee (run away from danger) and Defect (abandon one's country or cause for another).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Sybarite (भोग-विलासी): A person who loves luxury

2. Philanderer (स्त्रीलोलुप पुरुष): A man who has many casual affairs with women

3. Misanthrope (मानवद्वेषी): A person who dislikes or distrusts humankind

4. Philanthropist (परोपकारी): A person who does good deeds to help society

5. Nostalgia (विगत स्मृति/गृहविरह): A sentimental longing for the past

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A harsh, jarring mixture of discordant and confusing sounds.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Cacophony.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Cacophony" means a harsh, jarring mixture of discordant sounds, from the Greek “kakos” (bad) and “phone” (sound). (कर्कश ध्वनि)
◦ Example: The cacophony of car horns during rush hour gave her a headache.

 

• The root "-phony/phone" (from Greek “phone”, meaning sound) appears in many SSC words like euphony, telephone, and symphony, while the prefix "caco-" always signals something bad or unpleasant, as in cacography (bad handwriting) and cacology (poor choice of words).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Euphony (मधुर ध्वनि): A pleasing, harmonious sound, especially of spoken words.

 

• Option 2: Monotony (एकरसता): A tedious lack of variety or change, especially in sound or routine.

 

• Option 3: Symphony (स्वरमेल संगीत रचना): An elaborate musical composition for a full orchestra, typically in four movements.

 

NOTE

 

• Other words built on the Greek root "phone" (sound) frequently asked in SSC: Euphony (a pleasant sound), Homophone (a word sounding the same as another), Megaphone (a device to amplify the voice), Cacography (bad handwriting, from the same “caco-” prefix) and Polyphony (many voices or sounds together).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Ambidextrous (दोनों हाथों से समान काम करने वाला): Able to use both hands equally well

2. Nomad (घुमंतू): A person with no fixed home who moves from place to place

3. Vagabond (आवारा): A person who wanders from place to place without a home

4. Recluse (एकांतवासी): A person who lives in seclusion, avoiding others

5. Hermit (सन्यासी/वैरागी): A person living in solitude for religious reasons

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A poet, traditionally one who composed and recited epic or lyric verse.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Bard.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Bard" means a poet, traditionally one who composed and recited epic or lyric verse, often to musical accompaniment, from the Celtic/Gaelic “bard” (a tribal poet-singer). (कवि)
◦ Example: Shakespeare is often called the Bard of Avon.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: Orator (वक्ता): A skilled and eloquent public speaker.

 

• Option 3: Playwright (नाटककार): A person who writes plays for the theatre.

 

• Option 4: Laureate (पुरस्कृत कवि/विद्वान): A person honoured with an award for outstanding creative or intellectual achievement, especially in poetry.

 

NOTE

 

• Other words close in meaning to "Bard" frequently asked in SSC: Minstrel (a medieval singer/musician who told stories in verse), Laureate (a person honoured for outstanding creative work), Balladeer (a singer of ballads), Rhapsodist (one who recites epic poetry) and Troubadour (a medieval lyric poet and composer).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Loquacious (बातूनी): Very talkative

2. Taciturn (अल्पभाषी): Reserved and saying very little

3. Laconic (संक्षिप्तभाषी): Using very few words to express oneself

4. Garrulous (बकवादी): Excessively talkative, especially about trivial matters

5. Vociferous (चिल्लाकर बोलने वाला): Expressing one's opinions or feelings loudly

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A person who believes that war and violence are unjustifiable and who advocates peaceful resolution of disputes.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Pacifist.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Pacifist" means a person who believes that war and violence are unjustifiable and who advocates peace, from the Latin “pax” (peace) and “facere” (to make). (शांति प्रिय व्यक्ति)
◦ Example: As a committed pacifist, he refused to serve in the army.

 

• The suffix "-ist" commonly denotes a person who believes in or practises a particular doctrine, as in pacifist (believer in peace), socialist, and optimist.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Belligerent (युद्धरत): A person or country engaged in war or conflict; hostile and aggressive.

 

• Option 3: Mercenary (भाड़े का सैनिक): A professional soldier hired to serve in a foreign army.

 

• Option 4: Militant (उग्रवादी): A person favouring confrontational or violent methods in support of a political or social cause.

 

NOTE

 

• Other "-ist" words frequently asked in SSC: Optimist (one who expects the best), Pessimist (one who expects the worst), Anarchist (one who opposes all government), Egoist (one concerned only with self-interest), Altruist (one who acts for others' welfare) and Nihilist (one who rejects all religious and moral principles).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Verbose (शब्दाडंबरपूर्ण): Using more words than needed

2. Cognoscenti (पारखी/विशेषज्ञ): People with expert knowledge in a particular field

3. Erudite (विद्वान): Having great knowledge gained from reading and study

4. Bibliophile (पुस्तक प्रेमी): A lover or collector of books

5. Xenophobia (विदेशियों से भय/घृणा): Fear or hatred of foreigners or strangers

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A belief or opinion that is contrary to established religious doctrine or accepted tradition.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Heresy.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Heresy" means a belief or opinion that is contrary to established religious doctrine or accepted tradition, from the Greek “hairesis” (a taking, choice, or school of thought). (परम्पराओं के विपरीत विश्वास)
◦ Example: His views on the scriptures were condemned as heresy by the church.

 

• A person who holds or practises heresy is called a "heretic", just as a person who commits apostasy is called an "apostate."

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Blasphemy (ईशनिंदा): Irreverent speech or action concerning God or sacred things.

 

• Option 2: Sacrilege (पवित्र वस्तु का अनादर): The violation or misuse of something regarded as sacred.

 

• Option 4: Apostasy (धर्मत्याग): The formal abandonment or renunciation of a religious or political belief.

 

NOTE

 

• Other words related to unorthodox belief frequently asked in SSC: Apostasy (abandonment of one's religious faith), Blasphemy (irreverent speech about God), Sacrilege (violation of something sacred), Schism (a split between groups over doctrine) and Iconoclast (one who attacks cherished beliefs or traditions).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Claustrophobia (बंद स्थान का भय): An extreme fear of confined or enclosed spaces

2. Acrophobia (ऊंचाई का भय): An extreme fear of heights

3. Zoophobia (जानवरों का भय): An extreme fear of animals

4. Anarchist (अराजकतावादी): One who believes in the abolition of all government

5. Autocrat (निरंकुश शासक): A ruler who has absolute, unchecked power

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A person who falsely claims to have expert knowledge or skill, especially in medicine.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Charlatan.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Charlatan" means a person who falsely claims to have expert knowledge or skill, especially in medicine, from the Italian “ciarlatano” (one who chatters or prattles to sell wares). (झूठा वैद्य)
◦ Example: The self-styled healer turned out to be a charlatan with no medical training.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Impostor (पाखंडी/धोखेबाज़): A person who pretends to be someone else in order to deceive others.

 

• Option 2: Sycophant (चापलूस): A person who flatters others excessively to gain personal advantage.

 

• Option 3: Hypocrite (पाखंडी): A person who claims to have moral standards or beliefs that their own behaviour does not match.

 

NOTE

 

• Other words close in meaning to "Charlatan" frequently asked in SSC: Quack (a fraudulent doctor), Mountebank (a swindler who sells fake remedies), Impostor (one who pretends to be someone else), Fraud (a person who deceives for personal gain) and Trickster (a person who cheats or deceives others).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Demagogue (लोकरंजक नेता): A political leader who appeals to popular emotions and prejudices

2. Egoist (स्वार्थी/अहंवादी): A person concerned excessively with their own interests

3. Altruist (परोपकारी व्यक्ति): A person who acts selflessly for others' welfare

4. Optimist (आशावादी): One who tends to expect the best possible outcome

5. Pessimist (निराशावादी): One who tends to expect the worst possible outcome

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

Light, bantering talk or teasing, mocking in tone but meant in good humour.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Persiflage.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Persiflage" means light, bantering talk or teasing meant in good humour, from the French “persifler” (to banter or tease). (हल्की मजाकिया बातचीत)
◦ Example: Their conversation was full of persiflage rather than serious debate.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: Repartee (करारा उत्तर): A quick and witty reply or exchange of clever remarks.

 

• Option 3: Sarcasm (व्यंग्य): The use of remarks that clearly mean the opposite of what they say, used to mock or show contempt.

 

• Option 4: Rhetoric (अलंकारिक भाषण कला): The art of effective or persuasive speaking or writing.

 

NOTE

 

• Other words close in meaning to "Persiflage" frequently asked in SSC: Banter (playful, good-humoured teasing), Repartee (a witty, quick reply), Badinage (light, playful conversation), Raillery (good-humoured teasing or ridicule) and Wit (clever and quick humour).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Chauvinist (अंधराष्ट्रवादी): A person with an excessive or biased sense of loyalty to their group

2. Zealot (कट्टर समर्थक): A person who is fanatically committed to a cause

3. Iconoclast (परंपरा-विरोधी): One who attacks cherished beliefs or traditions

4. Puritan (कट्टर नैतिकतावादी): A person with strict moral or religious views

5. Hedonist (सुखवादी): One who believes pleasure is the most important thing in life

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A person who works to bring about social, political, or religious improvement within an existing system.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Reformer.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Reformer" means a person who works to bring about social, political, or religious improvement, from the Latin “re-” (again) and “formare” (to shape). (सुधारक)
◦ Example: Raja Ram Mohan Roy is remembered as a great social reformer.

 

• The prefix "re-" (meaning “again” or “back”) appears in many SSC words such as reform, revolt, and reclaim, generally indicating a return to, or repetition of, an action.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Revolutionary (क्रांतिकारी): A person who works for or supports radical, often forcible, political or social change.

 

• Option 3: Conservative (रूढ़िवादी): A person who is averse to change and supports traditional values and institutions.

 

• Option 4: Loyalist (वफादार): A person who remains loyal to an established government or ruler, especially during a revolt.

 

NOTE

 

• Other words related to social or political change frequently asked in SSC: Revolutionary (one who seeks radical or violent political change), Radical (one who favours extreme reform), Conservative (one who resists change and favours tradition), Loyalist (one who remains faithful to an established government) and Rebel (one who resists authority or control).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Ascetic (तपस्वी): One who practises strict self-denial for religious reasons

2. Stoic (अविचलित/धैर्यवान व्यक्ति): A person who endures hardship without complaint

3. Epicure (स्वादिष्ट भोजन प्रेमी): A person with refined taste in food and wine

4. Glutton (पेटू): A person who eats and drinks excessively

5. Teetotaller (पूर्ण मद्यत्यागी): A person who never drinks alcohol

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

Extremely old or old-fashioned, as if belonging to a bygone era.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Antediluvian.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Antediluvian" means extremely old or old-fashioned, as if belonging to a bygone era, from the Latin “ante” (before) and “diluvium” (flood) — literally “before the (biblical) flood.” (प्राचीन)
◦ Example: His antediluvian views on women in the workplace shocked the younger staff.

 

• The prefix "ante-" means before, as in antenatal (before birth), antecedent (something that came before), and antechamber (a room before the main one) — do not confuse it with "anti-", which means “against.”

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Venerable (पूज्य/श्रद्धेय): Accorded great respect, especially because of age, wisdom, or character.

 

• Option 2: Obsolete (अप्रचलित): No longer in use or produced; outdated, typically because something newer has replaced it.

 

• Option 4: Contemporary (समकालीन): Belonging to or occurring in the present time; modern.

 

NOTE

 

• Other "ante-" words frequently asked in SSC: Antenatal (before birth), Antecedent (a thing or event that preceded another), Anteroom (a small room leading to a main one), Antemeridian (before noon) and Antebellum (before a war, especially the American Civil War).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Renegade (विश्वासघाती/धर्मत्यागी): A person who deserts a cause or group to join another

2. Turncoat (पाला बदलने वाला): A person who changes their allegiance or party

3. Traitor (देशद्रोही): One who betrays their country, cause, or friend

4. Fugitive (भगोड़ा): A person fleeing from custody, arrest, or danger

5. Vagrant (आवारा): A person without a settled home who wanders idly

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A person who abandons or renounces their religious faith, political party, or set of beliefs.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Apostate.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Apostate" means a person who abandons or renounces their religious faith, political party, or set of beliefs, from the Greek “apostasis” (a standing away, defection), formed from “apo” (away from) and “stasis” (standing). (धर्मत्यागी)
◦ Example: He was branded an apostate after publicly renouncing his childhood faith.

 

• The related abstract noun is "apostasy" (the act of abandoning one's faith or principles), and the corresponding verb is "apostatize."

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Convert (धर्म-परिवर्तित व्यक्ति): A person who has changed their religious faith or set of beliefs.

 

• Option 2: Neophyte (नवदीक्षित): A person who is new to a subject, skill, or belief; a recent convert.

 

• Option 3: Fanatic (कट्टरपंथी): A person filled with excessive and uncritical zeal, especially concerning religion or politics.

 

NOTE

 

• Other words related to change of belief or loyalty frequently asked in SSC: Renegade (one who deserts a cause or group for another), Turncoat (one who changes allegiance or party), Convert (one who changes their religious faith), Heretic (one who holds a belief contrary to established doctrine) and Proselyte (a person who has converted to a new religion or belief).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Interregnum (राज-सत्ता का अंतराल): A period when there is no ruler or government in power

2. Utopia (काल्पनिक आदर्श स्थान): An imagined perfect place or society

3. Dystopia (दुखद कल्पित समाज): An imagined society characterized by great suffering or injustice

4. Anachronism (कालविपर्यय): Something placed in the wrong time period

5. Antiquarian (पुरातत्व प्रेमी): A person who studies or collects antiques and old objects

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A split or division between strongly opposed sections or factions, especially within a religious or political group, caused by differences in belief.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Schism.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Schism" means a split or division between strongly opposed sections or parties, typically within a religious or political group, from the Greek “skhisma” (a split or cleft), related to “skhizein” (to split). (मतभेद)
◦ Example: The disagreement over doctrine led to a schism within the church.

 

• The related adjective/noun for a person who causes or promotes such a division is "schismatic."

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: Consensus (सर्वसम्मति): General agreement reached among all members of a group.

 

• Option 3: Coalition (गठबंधन): A temporary alliance formed by distinct political parties or groups for joint action.

 

• Option 4: Faction (गुट): A small, organized dissenting group within a larger organization or party.

 

NOTE

 

• Other words describing division or disagreement frequently asked in SSC: Faction (a small dissenting group within a larger body), Rift (a serious disagreement between people or groups), Discord (disagreement or conflict), Dissension (disagreement leading to discord) and Cleavage (a division into two sharply opposed groups).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Novice (नौसिखिया): A person new to a skill or profession

2. Prodigy (अद्भुत प्रतिभाशाली व्यक्ति): A young person with exceptional talent

3. Virtuoso (निपुण कलाकार): A person highly skilled in an art, especially music

4. Maestro (उस्ताद/संगीत गुरु): A master, especially in music

5. Connoisseur (पारखी): An expert judge in matters of taste

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

Government or rule by the wealthy, or a class that controls a government because of its wealth.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Plutocracy.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Plutocracy" means government or rule by the wealthy, from the Greek “ploutos” (wealth) and “kratos” (power/rule). (धनिकों का शासन)
◦ Example: Critics argue that unchecked campaign funding is turning democracy into plutocracy.

 

• The suffix "-cracy" always denotes a form of government or rule, and the first part of the word tells us who or what holds the power.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Aristocracy (कुलीनतंत्र): Government or rule by a small privileged class, especially hereditary nobility.

 

• Option 3: Theocracy (धर्मतंत्र): A system of government in which religious leaders rule in the name of a god or religious doctrine.

 

• Option 4: Bureaucracy (नौकरशाही): A system of government administered by unelected officials organized in departments.

 

NOTE

 

• Other "-cracy" words frequently asked in SSC: Aristocracy (rule by a privileged, hereditary class), Theocracy (rule by religious authority), Bureaucracy (rule by unelected officials), Autocracy (rule by a single person with absolute power), Democracy (rule by the people) and Meritocracy (rule by those chosen for ability).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Dilettante (शौकिया कलाप्रेमी): A person with a superficial interest in an art or subject

2. Amateur (शौकिया): A person who engages in a pursuit without professional skill

3. Plagiarist (साहित्यिक चोर): One who copies another's work and claims it as their own

4. Forger (जालसाज़): One who makes fraudulent copies of documents, money, or art

5. Martinet (कठोर अनुशासक): A strict disciplinarian

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A state of temporary suspension or inactivity, expected to be resumed at a later time.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Abeyance.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Abeyance" means a state of temporary suspension or inactivity, expected to be resumed later, from the Anglo-Norman French “abeiance” (expectation) — originally a legal term for a title or right that was temporarily unclaimed. (स्थगन)
◦ Example: The plan was held in abeyance until further funds became available.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Adjournment (स्थगन): The postponement of a meeting or legal proceeding to a later time.

 

• Option 2: Recess (अवकाश): A temporary break or pause during the proceedings of a court, parliament, or school.

 

• Option 4: Hibernation (शीतनिद्रा): The dormant, inactive state in which certain animals spend the winter.

 

NOTE

 

• Other words close in meaning to "Abeyance" frequently asked in SSC: Moratorium (an officially authorised temporary suspension of an activity), Adjournment (the postponement of a meeting or proceeding), Recess (a temporary break in proceedings), Dormancy (a state of temporary inactivity) and Hiatus (a pause or gap in continuity).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Nihilist (शून्यवादी): One who rejects all religious and moral principles

2. Agnostic (अज्ञेयवादी): One who believes the existence of God is unknowable

3. Despot (निरंकुश शासक): A ruler with absolute, often cruel, power

4. Tyrant (अत्याचारी शासक): A cruel and oppressive ruler

5. Dictator (तानाशाह): A ruler with total power, often obtained by force

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A strong, formal expression of disapproval or criticism.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Censure.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Censure" means a strong expression of disapproval or formal criticism, from the Latin “censura” (judgment, assessment), itself from “censere” (to assess or judge). (निंदा)
◦ Example: The minister faced censure from the opposition for his remarks.

 

• The Latin root "cens-" relates to judging or assessing, and also appears in words like "census" (an official count/assessment) and "censor" (one who judges or suppresses).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Panegyric (प्रशस्ति): A formal public speech or piece of writing praising someone highly.

 

• Option 2: Adulation (चापलूसी): Excessive and often insincere admiration or praise.

 

• Option 3: Approbation (अनुमोदन): Approval or official sanction of something.

 

NOTE

 

• Other words close in meaning to "Censure" frequently asked in SSC: Reprimand (a formal rebuke), Rebuke (sharp criticism), Admonish (to warn or scold), Castigate (to criticise severely), and Reproach (an expression of disapproval).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Sybarite (भोग-विलासी): A person devoted to luxury and pleasure

2. Iconoclast (परंपरा भंजक): One who attacks cherished beliefs or traditions

3. Philistine (अरसिक व्यक्ति): A person indifferent or hostile to culture and the arts

4. Misanthrope (मानव द्वेषी): One who hates or distrusts mankind

5. Xenophobe (विदेशी-द्वेषी): A person who fears or hates foreigners

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A person who practices rigorous self-discipline and abstains from worldly pleasures, often for religious or spiritual reasons.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Ascetic.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Ascetic" means a person who practises rigorous self-discipline and abstains from worldly pleasures, from the Greek “asketes” (monk, hermit), itself from “askein” (to exercise or train). (तपस्वी / संयमी)
◦ Example: The old ascetic lived alone in the mountains, eating only what nature provided.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: Hedonist (सुखवादी): A person who believes pleasure is the most important pursuit in life.

 

• Option 3: Epicurean (सुखभोगी): One devoted to sensual enjoyment, especially fine food and comfort.

 

• Option 4: Voluptuary (विलासी): A person devoted to luxury and sensual pleasure.

 

NOTE

 

• Other words close in meaning to "Ascetic" frequently asked in SSC: Hermit (a person living in solitude for religious reasons), Recluse (one who avoids society), Puritan (a person with strict moral views), Stoic (one indifferent to pleasure and pain), and Anchorite (a religious recluse).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Nonagenarian (नब्बे से निन्यानवे वर्ष की आयु का व्यक्ति): A person aged between 90 and 99

2. Ambidextrous (दोनों हाथों से समान रूप से काम करने वाला): Able to use both hands equally well

3. Somnambulist (नींद में चलने वाला): A person who walks in their sleep

4. Loquacious (बातूनी): Very talkative

5. Taciturn (कम बोलने वाला): Reserved and saying little

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

The state of being no longer used or practiced; disuse.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Desuetude.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Desuetude" means the state of disuse; a condition of no longer being practised or used, from the Latin “desuetudo”, itself from “desuescere” (to become unaccustomed to). (अप्रचलन)
◦ Example: The old law had fallen into desuetude and was rarely enforced.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Abeyance (निलंबन): A state of temporary suspension, with the expectation of resumption.

 

• Option 3: Obsolescence (अप्रचलन / पुरातनता): The process of becoming outdated or no longer used, typically because something newer has replaced it.

 

• Option 4: Dormancy (निष्क्रियता): A state of temporary inactivity, as in a dormant volcano or dormant seed.

 

NOTE

 

• Other words close in meaning to "Desuetude" frequently asked in SSC: Obsolete (no longer in use), Defunct (no longer functioning or existing), Redundant (no longer needed), Archaic (very old and no longer used), and Moribund (in terminal decline, dying out).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Sycophant (चापलूस): A person who flatters others to gain advantage

2. Charlatan (ढोंगी / धोखेबाज़): A person who falsely claims special knowledge or skill

3. Vagabond (आवारा): A person who wanders without a settled home

4. Bibliophile (पुस्तक प्रेमी): A person who loves and collects books

5. Nihilist (शून्यवादी): One who believes life is meaningless and rejects moral principles

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A person who draws or produces maps.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Cartographer.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Cartographer" means a person who draws or produces maps, from the Greek “khartes” (map/papyrus) and “graphein” (to write/draw). (मानचित्रकार)
◦ Example: The cartographer spent months surveying the region before drawing the final map.

 

• The suffix "-grapher" (from Greek “graphein”, to write/draw) denotes a person who writes, draws, or records something, and the first part of the word tells us what is written or recorded — as in choreographer (dance), lexicographer (dictionaries), and calligrapher (ornamental writing).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Choreographer (नृत्य रचनाकार): A person who designs and arranges dance movements or sequences.

 

• Option 2: Lexicographer (शब्दकोश लेखक): A person who compiles or writes dictionaries.

 

• Option 4: Calligrapher (सुलेखक): A person skilled in decorative or artistic handwriting.

 

NOTE

 

• Other "-grapher" words frequently asked in SSC: Biographer (a person's life story), Photographer (photographs), Geographer (the earth's physical features), Stenographer (shorthand writing), Ethnographer (cultures and peoples), and Bibliographer (compiles lists of books).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Nomenclature (नामपद्धति): A system of names used in a particular field

2. Polyglot (बहुभाषाविद्): A person who knows and speaks several languages

3. Chauvinist (अंधराष्ट्रवादी / पक्षपाती): A person with an excessive, biased belief in the superiority of their own group

4. Zealot (कट्टर समर्थक): A person who is fanatically committed to a cause

5. Recluse (एकांतवासी): A person who lives in self-imposed isolation from others

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A person who eats and drinks to excess.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Glutton.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Glutton" means a person who eats and drinks to excess, from the Latin “gluttire” (to swallow, gulp down). (पेटू)
◦ Example: He ate three servings at dinner, behaving like a complete glutton.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Gourmet (भोजन का पारखी): A connoisseur of fine food and drink, valuing quality over quantity.

 

• Option 2: Epicure (स्वाद-पारखी): A person with refined and discriminating taste in food and wine.

 

• Option 3: Gourmand (भोजन प्रेमी): A person who enjoys eating good food, often in large quantities.

 

NOTE

 

• Other words close in meaning to "Glutton" frequently asked in SSC: Gormandizer (a person who eats greedily), Trencherman (a person with a hearty appetite), Voracious (having a very eager approach to eating), and Ravenous (extremely hungry, eating with great eagerness).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Martinet (अनुशासनप्रिय अधिकारी): A strict disciplinarian who demands rigid adherence to rules

2. Nomad (खानाबदोश): A person who moves from place to place without a permanent home

3. Voyeur (ताक-झांक करने वाला): A person who gains pleasure from secretly watching others

4. Plagiarist (साहित्यिक चोर): A person who copies another's work and passes it off as their own

5. Vandal (विध्वंसक): A person who deliberately destroys or damages property

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A statement that seems self-contradictory or absurd but may actually be true.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Paradox.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Paradox" means a statement that seems self-contradictory or absurd but may in fact be true, from the Greek “para” (contrary to) and “doxa” (opinion). (विरोधाभास)
◦ Example: "Less is more" is a famous paradox in design.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: Paradigm (प्रतिमान): A typical example or pattern of something; a model.

 

• Option 3: Anomaly (विसंगति): Something that deviates from what is standard, normal, or expected.

 

• Option 4: Analogy (उपमा): A comparison between two things, typically to explain or clarify something.

 

NOTE

 

• Other words close in meaning to "Paradox" frequently asked in SSC: Irony (an incongruity between expectation and reality), Contradiction (a statement opposing another), Enigma (something puzzling and mysterious), and Anachronism (something placed in the wrong historical period).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Mercenary (भाड़े का सैनिक): A soldier hired to fight for a foreign army for pay

2. Philanthropist (परोपकारी): A person who generously gives money or help to good causes

3. Egotist (स्वार्थी / अहंकारी): A person who is excessively self-centred

4. Altruist (परार्थी): A person unselfishly concerned for others' well-being

5. Puritan (कट्टर नैतिकतावादी): A person with strict moral or religious views

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

The criminal act of deliberately setting fire to property.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Arson.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Arson" means the criminal act of deliberately setting fire to property, from the Latin “ardere” (to burn), via Anglo-Norman French. (आगजनी)
◦ Example: The warehouse fire was later found to be a case of arson.

 

• A person who commits arson is called an "arsonist" — the suffix "-ist" denotes the person who performs or is devoted to the act named by the root word.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Larceny (चोरी): The unlawful taking of another person's property; theft.

 

• Option 3: Embezzlement (गबन): The fraudulent taking of funds or property entrusted to one's care.

 

• Option 4: Vandalism (तोड़फोड़): The deliberate destruction of or damage to property.

 

NOTE

 

• Other crime-related words frequently asked in SSC: Burglary (breaking into a building to commit theft), Perjury (lying under oath), Forgery (making a false document), Extortion (obtaining something through force or threats), and Homicide (the killing of a human being).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Turncoat (पाला बदलने वाला): A person who deserts one party or cause for another

2. Traitor (देशद्रोही): A person who betrays their country or a trust

3. Anarchist (अराजकतावादी): A person who believes in the abolition of all government

4. Autocrat (निरंकुश शासक): A ruler who has absolute power

5. Bureaucrat (नौकरशाह): An official in a government department, often rigidly following rules

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

An abnormal fear of public speaking.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Glossophobia.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Glossophobia" means an abnormal fear of public speaking, from the Greek “glossa” (tongue, language) and “phobos” (fear). (सार्वजनिक बोलने का भय)
◦ Example: Her hands trembled before every presentation because of her glossophobia.

 

• The suffix "-phobia" always denotes an irrational or excessive fear of something, and the first part of the word tells us what is feared.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Claustrophobia (बंद स्थान का भय): An abnormal fear of confined or enclosed spaces.

 

• Option 2: Acrophobia (ऊंचाई का भय): An abnormal fear of heights.

 

• Option 4: Xenophobia (विदेशियों से भय / घृणा): An intense dislike or fear of foreigners or strangers.

 

NOTE

 

• Other "-phobia" words frequently asked in SSC: Arachnophobia (spiders), Agoraphobia (open or crowded public spaces), Hydrophobia (water), Nyctophobia (darkness), Pyrophobia (fire), and Photophobia (light).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Plutocrat (धनिकतंत्रवादी): A person whose power derives from wealth

2. Theocrat (धर्मतंत्रवादी शासक): A ruler who governs in the name of a deity or religious authority

3. Vagrant (आवारा / बेघर व्यक्ति): A person without a settled home or regular work

4. Fugitive (भगोड़ा): A person who has escaped from captivity or is in hiding

5. Deserter (भगोड़ा सैनिक): A soldier who abandons duty without permission

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

An extremely large, countless number of something.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Myriad.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Myriad" means an extremely large, countless number of something, from the Greek “myrias” (ten thousand, a vast number). (अनगिनत)
◦ Example: The night sky was filled with a myriad of stars.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Plethora (अधिकता): An excessive or overabundant amount of something.

 

• Option 2: Multitude (बड़ी संख्या): A large number of people or things, especially people gathered together.

 

• Option 3: Paucity (अल्पता): A smallness or insufficiency of number or quantity; scarcity.

 

NOTE

 

• Other words close in meaning to "Myriad" frequently asked in SSC: Innumerable (too many to count), Countless (very great in number), Legion (a very great number), and Copious (abundant in quantity) — while its opposites Paucity (scarcity) and Dearth (a lack) are also frequently tested.

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Novice (नौसिखिया): A person new to and inexperienced in a field or activity

2. Connoisseur (पारखी): An expert judge in matters of taste, especially in the arts or food

3. Prodigy (विलक्षण प्रतिभा): A young person with exceptional talents or abilities

4. Renegade (विद्रोही / धर्मत्यागी): A person who deserts a group or cause for an opposing one

5. Maverick (स्वतंत्र विचारों वाला व्यक्ति): An unorthodox or independent-minded person

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A person who publicly disagrees with and opposes an official policy or authority, especially a political one.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Dissident.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Dissident" means a person who publicly disagrees with and opposes an official policy or authority, from the Latin “dissidere” (to sit apart, disagree), from “dis-” (apart) and “sedere” (to sit). (असहमत व्यक्ति)
◦ Example: The dissident was imprisoned for openly criticising the government.

 

• The Latin prefix "dis-" denotes negation, separation, or opposition, and appears in similar words such as dissent (to disagree), discord (disagreement), and dissonance (a lack of harmony).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: Loyalist (निष्ठावान समर्थक): A person who remains firmly loyal to the established government or ruler, especially during opposition or rebellion.

 

• Option 3: Diplomat (राजनयिक): An official who conducts negotiations and maintains relations on behalf of their country.

 

• Option 4: Advocate (समर्थक): A person who publicly supports or recommends a particular cause, policy, or person.

 

NOTE

 

• Other words close in meaning to "Dissident" frequently asked in SSC: Rebel (one who resists authority), Dissenter (one who disagrees with an official view), Nonconformist (one who does not conform to accepted norms), Maverick (an unorthodox, independent thinker), and Renegade (one who deserts a cause).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Misogynist (स्त्री-द्वेषी): A person who dislikes or is prejudiced against women

2. Misandrist (पुरुष-द्वेषी): A person who dislikes or is prejudiced against men

3. Pyromaniac (अग्नि-उन्माद से ग्रस्त व्यक्ति): A person with an obsessive urge to set fires

4. Kleptomaniac (चोरी करने की उन्मादी प्रवृत्ति वाला व्यक्ति): A person with an uncontrollable urge to steal

5. Megalomaniac (आत्ममुग्ध सत्ता-लोलुप व्यक्ति): A person obsessed with their own power or importance

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

An offensive display of excessive pride and self-importance, often with contempt for others.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Arrogance.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Arrogance" means an offensive display of excessive pride and self-importance, often with contempt for others, from the Latin “arrogare” (to claim for oneself), from “ad-” (to) and “rogare” (to ask). (घमंड)
◦ Example: His arrogance made him dismiss everyone else's opinions.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Humility (विनम्रता): A modest and low view of one's own importance; the opposite of arrogance.

 

• Option 3: Diffidence (संकोच): Shyness or modesty resulting from a lack of self-confidence.

 

• Option 4: Reverence (श्रद्धा): Deep respect or admiration felt towards someone or something.

 

NOTE

 

• Other words close in meaning to "Arrogance" frequently asked in SSC: Hubris (excessive pride or self-confidence), Haughtiness (arrogant superiority), Vanity (excessive pride in appearance or achievements), Conceit (excessive pride in oneself), and Insolence (disrespectful or arrogant behaviour).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Neophyte (नौसिखिया / नवदीक्षित): A person who is new to a subject, skill, or belief

2. Skeptic (संशयवादी): A person inclined to question or doubt accepted beliefs

3. Cynic (निंदक): A person who believes people are motivated chiefly by self-interest

4. Pessimist (निराशावादी): A person who always expects the worst outcome

5. Idealist (आदर्शवादी): A person who is guided by ideals rather than practical considerations

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A feeling of listlessness and dissatisfaction arising from a lack of occupation or excitement; boredom.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Ennui.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Ennui" means a feeling of listlessness and dissatisfaction arising from a lack of occupation or excitement; boredom, from the French “ennui”, ultimately from the Latin “in odio” (in hatred/hateful to). (ऊब)
◦ Example: A deep sense of ennui settled over him after weeks of the same routine.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Lethargy (सुस्ती): A lack of energy and enthusiasm; physical or mental sluggishness.

 

• Option 2: Melancholy (विषाद): A deep, pensive, and long-lasting feeling of sadness.

 

• Option 4: Nostalgia (अतीत की यादें): A sentimental longing or wistful affection for the past.

 

NOTE

 

• Other words close in meaning to "Ennui" frequently asked in SSC: Boredom (a state of weariness from lack of interest), Tedium (the state of being tedious or dull), Languor (a pleasant tiredness or weakness), and Weariness (extreme tiredness).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Philatelist (डाक-टिकट संग्रहकर्ता): A person who collects postage stamps

2. Numismatist (सिक्का संग्रहकर्ता): A person who collects or studies coins

3. Ornithologist (पक्षीविज्ञानी): A person who studies birds

4. Entomologist (कीटविज्ञानी): A person who studies insects

5. Philanderer (स्त्रीलंपट पुरुष): A man who habitually has casual love affairs with women

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A formal speech or piece of writing that praises someone or something highly.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Encomium.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Encomium" means a formal speech or piece of writing that praises someone or something highly, from the Greek “enkomion” (a laudatory ode), from “en-” (in) and “komos” (celebration, revel). (प्रशंसा / स्तुति)
◦ Example: The retiring professor received an encomium from his students at the farewell.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Elegy (शोकगीत): A mournful poem, typically a lament for the dead.

 

• Option 2: Eulogy (श्रद्धांजलि भाषण): A speech or piece of writing that praises someone who has died.

 

• Option 3: Epitaph (समाधि-लेख): Words inscribed on a tombstone in memory of the deceased.

 

NOTE

 

• Other words close in meaning to "Encomium" frequently asked in SSC: Panegyric (a formal public speech of praise), Tribute (an act or statement showing gratitude or admiration), Accolade (an award or praise for an achievement), and Commendation (formal praise).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Sciolist (छद्म विद्वान): A person who pretends to be knowledgeable but has only superficial understanding

2. Polymath (बहुज्ञ व्यक्ति): A person with extensive knowledge across many different fields

3. Dilettante (शौकिया कलाप्रेमी): A person who dabbles in a subject without serious commitment

4. Autodidact (स्वयं-शिक्षित व्यक्ति): A person who is self-taught

5. Savant (असाधारण ज्ञानी व्यक्ति): A person with profound knowledge or ability in a particular area
